parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. The division is among the most protective: public-accommodations and employment bans on gender identity/expression, hate-crime coverage, gender-identity custody policy (housing, strip searches), a healthcare shield law, open M/F/X documents, and a 'Most Protective' ranking. But the traveller meets the hostile federal layer at every journey stage: March/Nov 2025 passport marker regime in force, visa cable instructing refusal on doubt about sex with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration, trans-athlete entry tag, airport pat-down outing risk, federal-building facility bans, and conversion-therapy policy in federal custody. Litigation is unresolved, so federal exposures are live and universal while state protections are strong but not documented as enforcement-tested for visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal regime: X markers barred for new issues; sex-marker restrictions upheld Nov 2025; visa cable orders refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and invites fraud/lifetime-ineligibility analysis; reports of passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded; allied governments issued advisories. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: State offers M/F/X on its own licences and birth certificates, but these do not govern federal entry documents for a visitor. Litigation pending; existing X-marker passports valid to expiry. Partial, uncertain protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at the border can escalate from state-level acceptance to federal refusal or fraud review, moving the encounter from the protective division layer into the hostile federal layer. Status: documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal custody: corrections-bureau conversion-therapy policy from 2026 (hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees; trans men targeted. Documented but low-probability for an ordinary tourist.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division policy (since 1 July 2018) requires custody treatment by gender identity including strip searches, housing, clothing and commissary. Documented and in force for state custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A trans visitor stopped for a state offence receives identity-respecting placement; any transfer to federal custody (immigration, federal charge) exposes them to the federal regime, which is the harsher operative rule. Status: documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal buildings (airports, courthouses, national sites, federally funded single-sex facilities) are barred to identity-congruent use under the Jan 2025 order; nationally, 22 units restrict facilities and 4 criminalise in some circumstances, with one documented arrest. Documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division bans facility discrimination in public places and holds no mapped facility ban; ranked in the 15-member 'Most Protective' tier. Documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Everyday venues (hotels, shops, restaurants, state buildings) are protected, but entering a federal building re-imposes the birth-sex rule; the facility exposure is real yet geographically bounded. Status: documented.

care_services.exposure: Federal: funding freeze, proposed public-insurance bar for under-18s, subpoena of youth gender-care records, crisis-lifeline LGBTQ service shut-down; corrections hormone withdrawal. Documented federally, mostly resident/minor-facing.
care_services.protection: Division 2022 shield law protects patients and providers from out-of-state charges — directly relevant to a visiting family; anti-discrimination covers goods and services; hate-crime law strengthened (consolidated provisions effective 1 Oct 2026). Documented.
care_services.interaction: A visitor (or parent) seeking ordinary or gender-related care in the division is shielded and served; emergency care in a federal facility could re-encounter hostile federal funding rules. Not documented as applied to visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing is hostile: 'gender ideology' removal, law-enforcement directive on schools, counterterrorism language on 'radically pro-transgender' groups, compared by advocates to genocide stages; 66% public support for ASAB-on-documents laws. Documented nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division hate-crime statute covers gender identity/expression with added penalties (earlier provisions operative before 1 Oct 2026); discrimination ban since 2011; 2019 repeal of gay-panic defence. Documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State law enforcement is obligated to treat identity-motivated crime as a hate crime, cushioning federal threat-framing at street level; federal agencies operating in-state follow the hostile posture. Status: documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal executive orders criminalise teachers facilitating social transition, label youth care 'mutilation', and back national funding cuts; 27 units ban youth care; proposed insurance bar. Threat is primarily resident/school-facing.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield law directly protects a visiting family from care lawful here but banned at home; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2017; anti-bullying statute covers gender identity/expression. Documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent and minor are protected within the division by the shield law, but crossing into a restricting unit or federal jurisdiction removes that protection; document rules apply equally to minors' accompanying adults. Status: documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific count of anti-trans violence or killings exists; national bias statistics show sexual-orientation bias at 1/7–1/5 of single-bias incidents; airport screening pat-downs risk outing. Undocumented at division level, uncertain nationally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute with identity coverage and June 2026 strengthening; public-accommodations enforcement mechanism exists; discrimination ban in goods/services since 2011. Documented on paper; enforcement record for visitors not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of a division violence count in an otherwise heavily documented dossier is weakly positive but not proof; recourse exists but no visitor-facing enforcement outcomes are shown. Status: not_documented for incidence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal passport suit and EO challenges unresolved; practical exposure shifts with injunctions; no documented visitor enforcement outcomes for division accommodations law; airport/anomaly-resolution experiences undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport/name rules; active civil-liberties litigation; shield law, accommodations statute, hate-crime law and custody policy all in force; 'Most Protective' ranking built from tracked bills.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist at both layers but federal remedies have not stopped the document regime, while division remedies are untested against federal action; unknowns are open questions, not exposures. Status: documented as mixed.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this anchor. Veluna imposes a universal birth-sex facility rule across all public buildings with courts confirming exclusion and no visitor exemption. Here the exclusion reaches only federal buildings, while the division affirmatively bans identity-based service denial and ranks 'Most Protective'; the traveller's everyday exposure is materially narrower and remedy-backed.

Similar, tilted by scope. Ovessa shows recurring humiliating airport questioning partially corrected. Here the airport/border exposure is national, systemic and currently in force (marker regime upheld, refusal-on-doubt cable), yet the division adds in-force accommodations, custody and shield protections Ovessa's dossier lacks; comparable net position.

Higher than this anchor. Norvella rests on a corrected airport incident, routine service enforcement and identity-respecting wards with no hostile national document regime. Our dossier's federal layer — passport restrictions, visa-refusal guidance, federal facility bans, custody conversion policy — is live and universal, outweighing Norvella's single friction point.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is two-tiered. Within the division, a trans visitor's ordinary journey — hotels, restaurants, shops, state buildings, state custody, medical care — is governed by in-force anti-discrimination, hate-crime, custody and shield provisions, with open M/F/X documents and a top protective ranking. Above that sits a federal regime that the dossier shows currently operative: passport marker restrictions upheld in Nov 2025, visa adjudication instructions to refuse on doubt about sex with possible lifetime fraud findings, trans-athlete entry tags, airport pat-down outing risk, birth-sex use of federal single-sex facilities, and conversion-therapy practice in federal custody. Litigation is pending, so federal exposure is real but partially checked. Nothing documents organised targeting or violence against visitors; the division violence count is simply absent. The rating therefore sits mid-scale: strong local protection continuously punctuated by an unavoidable, unresolved federal document-and-facility layer that dominates the border, airport and federal-building stages, with unknowns treated as open questions rather than exposures.
